alt: AS Level is Papers 1 and 2; the full A Level adds Papers 3 and 4. Paper 4 lasts 1 hour 45 minutes, is worth 70 marks (two 35-mark essays) and 29% of the A Level, and candidates answer two essays from different sections.
caption: Paper 4 is the A Level-only finale: two 35-mark essays from two different sections.

alt: Section A Globalisation covers syllabus headings 7 and 8, Section B Media covers headings 9 and 10, and Section C Religion covers headings 11 and 12.
caption: Each lettered section draws on two numbered syllabus headings.

alt: For globalisation, global influence is weighed against the revival of local identities; for media, direct effects against active audiences; for religion, cohesion against change and conflict; and secularisation is weighed as a debated question.
caption: High marks come from weighing two competing explanations, not describing one.

after: ## Worked example: applying methods to a media question
alt: A strong answer selects a named perspective on media influence, applies it to young people’s identities, suggests a research method and notes a limitation of that method. A weak answer only describes social media and asserts it has a big influence.
caption: Strong Paper 4 answers link a theoretical claim to how it could be researched.

alt: Five common Paper 4 mistakes paired with fixes: treating globalisation as only economic, presenting one media theory as true, treating secularisation as settled, ignoring research methods and using only old examples.
caption: Each common mistake has a simple fix: widen, weigh, debate, link to methods, update.
